lines.japanese: とても無駄な時間を過ごしてしまった。
lines.english: What a colossal waste of time.

lines.japanese: くそ、あのバカップルのせいだ。ちくしょう、ハゲ！　ハゲ！　ハゲ！　貧乳！　ハゲ！
lines.english: Dammit. It was that idiot couple's fault. Baldy! Baldy! Baldy! Flat-chest! Baldy!

lines.japanese: いや、やめとこう。今日のところは、やつらのせいばかりとも言いきれない。
lines.english: No. Forget it. Today, at least, I couldn't blame everything on them.

lines.japanese: 大して親しい仲でもないのにさっさと立ちさらなかったのは、きっと俺のせこい時間稼ぎだ。
lines.english: We weren't even close. The fact that I hadn't walked away sooner was probably just my own pathetic attempt to stall for time.

lines.japanese: 品のないテーマパークみたいな風俗ビル群を尻目に、俺は柳木原の外れへと向かった。
lines.english: Leaving the adult-entertainment buildings behind me, clustered like some tawdry theme park, I headed toward the edge of Yanagihara.

lines.japanese: 目指すは最後のツテ。食うに困ったときの最終手段。
lines.english: I was going to the last person I could turn to. My final resort whenever I was too broke to eat.

lines.japanese: だから俺は、このばっちい通勤路を歩いているといつも気が滅入ってくるんだ。まるで不登校児童の心境。あそこにはあまり行きたく──
lines.english: That was why this filthy route to work always depressed me. I felt like a schoolkid dreading the walk to school. I really didn't want to go there—

lines.japanese: 「グァウッ！　ガウワウ！」
lines.english: “Grrarf! Rarf, rarf!”

lines.japanese: 突然の吠え声だった。俺は反射的に飛びのいていた。
lines.english: A bark exploded out of nowhere. I sprang aside on instinct.

lines.japanese: 着地と同時に腰を低く落とし、こぶしをふたつ顎の先に掲げる──
lines.english: I landed low, both fists raised before my chin—

lines.japanese: ──が、相手がただの薄汚れた雑種犬と知れたので緊張を解いた。
lines.english: —then saw that my opponent was nothing more than a filthy mutt and relaxed.

lines.japanese: 「ちっ……ああくそ、ビビっちゃったじゃねーか、てめ」
lines.english: “Tch... Goddammit. You scared me, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「ウゥゥゥ……」
lines.english: “Grrrr...”

lines.japanese: しかし、やつは警戒を解かない。狭い路地裏の窪みには、雀荘の名前が書かれた青いポリバケツが、中身を吐きだして横倒しになっていた。
lines.english: It remained on guard. In a recess of the narrow alley, a blue plastic trash bin bearing the name of a mahjong parlor lay on its side, its contents vomited across the ground.

lines.japanese: 「ウーじゃねーよ馬鹿。犬かてめえは。盗らねえよ、盗るかよそんなん」
lines.english: “Quit growling, idiot. What are you, a dog? I'm not stealing it. Why the hell would I want any of that?”

lines.japanese: しかしそいつは、四つの足をひび割れたコンクリートに据えて、なお低く喉を鳴らしつづける。俺の何が気に食わないんだか。畜生のくせに、人間みたいな腐った目をしていた。
lines.english: But the creature planted all four paws on the cracked concrete and kept up the low rumble in its throat. What was its problem with me? An animal, yet it had the same rotten eyes as a human being.

lines.japanese: 「ヤロウ……」
lines.english: “You bastard...”

lines.japanese: 気に入らない。やはり俺は構えを取った。こんな目でひとを睨むやつのために、わざわざ迂回してやる義理はない。
lines.english: I didn’t like that. I raised my guard again. I wasn’t about to take a detour for anything that glared at me with eyes like those.

lines.japanese: もともと俺は動物が好きな方じゃない。やつらは群れの中で順位付けをする。相手が自分より上か下かで態度を変える。仲間同士で馬鹿じゃねえの。そういうすべての動物が好きじゃない。
lines.english: I had never particularly liked animals. They ranked everyone in the pack, then changed their behavior according to who stood above or below them. What kind of idiots did that to their own companions? I disliked every animal that did.

lines.japanese: 「しつけがなってねーな。一度痛い目見とくか、ビッチ」
lines.english: “Someone didn't train you properly. Want me to teach you a painful lesson, bitch?”

lines.japanese: 俺は挑発するように摺り足で前へ進んだ。服従を強いる獣の咆哮。うるせえ、小物。
lines.english: I shuffled forward in provocation. The beast roared, demanding my submission. Shut up, runt.

lines.japanese: 俺の三歩目で、我慢できずにやつが動いた。前に置いておいた囮の左足めがけ、跳ねるように飛びかかってきた。
lines.english: On my third step, it lost patience and sprang at the left leg I had planted forward as bait.

lines.japanese: 黄ばんだ歯牙が間近に迫った瞬間、俺は後ろに隠していた右足を一気に前へ振りぬいた。
lines.english: The instant those yellowed fangs came near, I whipped my hidden right leg forward in one clean stroke.

lines.japanese: 「キャウンッ！」
lines.english: “Yelp!”

lines.japanese: 宙に弾かれ、やつが甲高い雌犬の声で鳴いた。
lines.english: Knocked into the air, it let out the shrill yelp of a frightened bitch.

lines.japanese: 猛々しく示威の叫びをあげていた四つ足のチンピラは、いまや自らが広げた残飯の上で、都会の泥土に汚れた腹を晒していた。
lines.english: The four-legged punk that had been roaring its threats so fiercely now lay atop the garbage it had scattered, baring a belly stained with city filth.

lines.japanese: やつは慌てて起きあがると、捨て台詞ひとつ残さずにギャロップで走りさっていった。
lines.english: It scrambled upright and galloped away without so much as a parting shot.

lines.japanese: 「クソが……きゃうんじゃねーよ、萌えキャラかてめえは。二足歩行なめんなコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Piece of shit... Don’t yelp at me. What are you, some cute anime character? Don’t underestimate bipedal locomotion, asshole.”

lines.japanese: まあ、実際ほとんど力は入れないでおいたから、べつに怪我はしてないだろう。さすがに、家ダニやゴキブリぐらいならともかく、哺乳類相手に過剰防衛は寝覚めが悪い。
lines.english: In truth, I had kept almost all the force out of the kick, so it probably wasn’t hurt. Mites and cockroaches were one thing, but I’d feel guilty about using excessive force against another mammal.

lines.japanese: つーか、なあ、ワンワン相手にマジんなっても。
lines.english: Besides, getting serious over a doggie? Come on.

lines.japanese: ……半マジだったけど。
lines.english: ...Though I had been half-serious.

lines.japanese: 「勝利のあとはなぜか虚しい」
lines.english: “Why does victory feel so hollow?”

lines.japanese: 俺は溜息をつきながら、ゲロ臭い路地裏を先へ進んだ。あいつらと違って、万物の霊長にはいろいろやることがあるんだ。
lines.english: With a sigh, I continued down the vomit-reeking alley. Unlike the beasts, the crown of creation had all kinds of things to do.

lines.japanese: それから花水木通りをしばらく歩きつづけた。
lines.english: I walked along Flowering Dogwood Street for a while.

lines.japanese: ぶっとい幹線道路の両脇から、繁華街のぎらついた輝きが徐々に減っていった。その分ひっそりと夜を照らす水銀灯の白い光と、ゆるやかな速度で俺を追いこしてゆくテールランプが目立ちはじめた。
lines.english: The glitter of the entertainment district gradually thinned along both sides of the broad arterial road. In its place, the quiet white glow of mercury lamps and the taillights overtaking me at an easy pace began to stand out.

lines.japanese: 年の瀬が近付いて、道路のあちこちが掘りかえされてる。アスファルトの大河に並んだ蛍光色のパイロンは、なんだか季節はずれの灯篭流しみたいだ。
lines.english: The year was drawing to a close, and roads had been dug up everywhere. Fluorescent pylons lined the river of asphalt like lanterns set afloat out of season.

lines.japanese: 俺は自分を売りこむため、工事現場のおっさんたちに声をかけてまわった。
lines.english: I went from worksite to worksite, asking the men there if they could use me.

lines.japanese: 真夜中の就職活動。リクルートスーツは擦り切れたジーンズにくたびれたＮ－２Ｂ。アウトレットのバーゲンで買った安物のスニーカーが、いつになく重かった。
lines.english: A midnight job hunt. My interview suit: frayed jeans and a battered N-2B. The cheap sneakers I'd bought in an outlet sale felt heavier than ever.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、おまえか。久しぶりだな」
lines.english: “Oh. It's you. Been a while.”

lines.japanese: 防護柵越しに声をかけると、顔じゅう髭だらけの現場監督は愛想のない声で応えた。白い息を吐きながら、茶ばんだタオルで汗を拭っている。俺は唾を飲みこみ背筋を伸ばした。
lines.english: When I called across the safety barrier, the site foreman—a face almost entirely made of beard—answered without warmth. His breath fogging white, he wiped away sweat with a brown-stained towel. I swallowed and straightened my back.

lines.japanese: 「あの。いま、ちょっといいすか」
lines.english: “Um. You got a minute?”

lines.japanese: おっさんのヘソのあたりに目を落として伺うと、やつは低い声で入れと言った。
lines.english: I lowered my gaze to somewhere around the man's navel as I asked. In a low voice, he told me to come in.

lines.japanese: 俺はオレンジ色のＡ字型バリケードをまたいで封鎖レーンの内側へ入り、もし人手が足りてなければ使ってほしいということを説明した。おっさんにはこれまでも過去何度か世話になっていた。
lines.english: I stepped over an orange A-frame barricade into the closed lane and explained that if they were short-handed, I wanted him to put me to work. He had hired me several times before.

lines.japanese: 「どすか」
lines.english: “How about it?”
“What!?”

lines.japanese: おっさんがしかめた顔を横にして、俺に耳を向ける。エンジン発電機の騒がしい唸り。俺は声を張った。
lines.english: The man turned his scowling face aside and offered me one ear. An engine generator throbbed and roared nearby. I raised my voice.

lines.japanese: 「どうっすか」
lines.english: “How about it?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ！　ちょっと待ってろ！」
lines.english: “Right! Wait there!”

lines.japanese: 車道は片側三車線のうち、中央分離帯ぎわの一線だけが封鎖されていた。その細長い現場がおっさんたちの神聖なる職場だ。
lines.english: The road had three lanes in each direction, but only the lane beside the median was closed. That long, narrow worksite was the men's sacred ground.

lines.japanese: ヒゲのおっさんは聖域をまっすぐ小走りで進み、やがて、アスファルトを薄く切りひらいて砂利が剥きだしになっている区画の縁で立ちどまった。
lines.english: The bearded man trotted straight through the sanctuary and stopped at the edge of a section where the top layer of asphalt had been cut away, leaving the gravel exposed.

lines.japanese: 地面をならしている年若いアルバイトたちにでかい声で呼びかけ、俺の方を指差す。憂鬱そうに傾いていた数個のヘルメットが、一斉にこっちを向いた。
lines.english: He shouted to the young laborers leveling the ground and pointed at me. Several dispirited helmets turned my way at once.

lines.japanese: ハロゲン投光機の容赦ない白光に晒されていた俺には、逃げ場がない。会釈する振りをしてそのまま俯いた。見られることには慣れてない。俺はストリッパーじゃないんだ。
lines.english: Exposed beneath the merciless white glare of the halogen floodlights, I had nowhere to hide. I pretended to bow and kept my head down. I wasn't used to being watched. I wasn't a stripper.

lines.japanese: えぐりとったアスファルトを満載したダンプが、低いうなりを上げて動きだす。その脇を平然とすり抜けて、ヒゲ監督が小走りで戻ってきた。
lines.english: A dump truck loaded with torn-up asphalt rumbled into motion. The bearded foreman slipped calmly past it and trotted back.

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、名前なんだっけ」
lines.english: “What was your name again?”

lines.japanese: 「成田」
lines.english: “Narita.”

lines.japanese: 「です」
lines.english: “Sir.”

lines.japanese: 「あーあー、成田な。履歴書持ってきたか？」
lines.english: “Right, right. Narita. You bring a résumé?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 「免許証は？」
lines.english: “Driver's license?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ。免許持ってないすから」
lines.english: “No. I don't have one.”

lines.japanese: おっさんは眉間にしわを寄せた。
lines.english: The man furrowed his brow.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そういやそうだったな」
lines.english: “Right. I remember now.”

lines.japanese: 前科者か不法入国者でも見るような目で一瞥された。しかし、有難いことにそれだけだった。
lines.english: He gave me the kind of look reserved for an ex-con or an illegal immigrant. Thankfully, that was all.

lines.japanese: 「ま、いいか」
lines.english: “Good enough.”

lines.japanese: どうでもよさそうに一言つぶやいて、あとは作業の細かい説明に入った。何度目かの縁だ、おっさんは分かってる。俺は大した資格や技能を持ってないけど、雑用係としちゃかなりタフで真面目で使える方なんだ。
lines.english: He muttered the words as though none of it mattered, then moved on to the details of the job. We had history; he knew me. I had no real qualifications or skills, but as an extra pair of hands I was tough, diligent, and useful.

lines.japanese: 「成田、作業着は持ってきてんのか」
lines.english: “Narita, you bring work clothes?”

lines.japanese: 「うす」
lines.english: “Yessir.”

lines.japanese: 俺は中身の詰まったスポーツバッグをその場で担ぎなおした。
lines.english: I hitched the bulging sports bag higher on my shoulder.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、とっととその辺で着替えてこい」
lines.english: “Then hurry up and change somewhere around here.”

lines.japanese: そう命じて、ヒゲ監督は自分の持ち場に戻った。向けられた視線がなくなって、俺はようやく肩を下げた──肩が上がってることに気付いたのはそのときだったけど。
lines.english: With that order, the bearded foreman returned to his post. Once his eyes were off me, my shoulders finally dropped—though only then did I realize I had been holding them up.

lines.japanese: 頭上の高速道路を支えるドでかい橋脚の陰で、俺は手早く着替えを済ませた。路地裏の野良犬みたいな色をした作業着は、いつかの汗が染みこんでいて少し臭かった。
lines.english: In the shadow of a colossal pier supporting the expressway overhead, I changed quickly. My work clothes were the same dingy color as the alley stray and smelled faintly of old sweat.

lines.japanese: タオルは以前ラブホテルの清掃作業を手伝ったとき、パートのおばちゃんからこっそりもらったものだ。マフラー代わりに首に巻きつけておく。肌に馴染むまで少しちくちくした。
lines.english: The towel was something a part-time cleaner had slipped me when I once helped clean a love hotel. I wound it around my neck in place of a scarf. It prickled until it settled against my skin.

lines.japanese: 顎の下で安全帽のストラップをはめながら、俺はヒゲ監督の元へ走った。走るのは基本だ。飛び込みのバイト小僧にちんたら歩いてる暇はない。と前に怒鳴られたことがある。
lines.english: Fastening the hard-hat strap beneath my chin, I ran back to the bearded foreman. Running was basic. A walk-in temp had no business strolling around—that was something I'd been shouted at for before.

lines.japanese: 「そうだな、そしたらまずは──」
lines.english: “Let's see. First—”

lines.japanese: 指示を仰ぐと、おっさんは軍手の甲で額を拭いながら現場を見渡した。
lines.english: When I asked for instructions, the man wiped his forehead with the back of his work glove and surveyed the site.

lines.japanese: 「──おし。あっこら辺落っこってるガラ、ぜんぶ詰めて上逃がしとけ。ネコその辺あっから」
lines.english: “—Right. Bag all that rubble lying around over there and move it up out of the way. Wheelbarrow's around there somewhere.”

lines.japanese: （訳：ショベルカーが取りこぼしていった欠片を拾いあつめ、すべて麻袋に詰めてトラックの荷台へ運んでおいてください。一輪車の使用を許可します）
lines.english: (Translation: Please gather the fragments left behind by the excavator, pack them all into burlap sacks, and carry them to the bed of the truck. You are authorized to use a wheelbarrow.)

lines.japanese: 「うす」
lines.english: “Yessir.”

lines.japanese: 俺はゴム引きの軍手に指を通しながら、スニーカーで一輪車の元へ走った。安全靴じゃないのは少しばかり心もとなかった。
lines.english: Pulling on my rubber-coated work gloves, I ran in my sneakers toward the wheelbarrow. Not having steel-toed boots made me a little uneasy.

lines.japanese: ざっくり抉られた路面の周りには、乾燥した犬のフンみたいな塊がごろごろ転がっていた。油圧式ショベルで掬いきれなかったアスファルトの小片だ。
lines.english: Dry lumps like dog crap lay scattered around the roughly gouged road surface: small pieces of asphalt the hydraulic shovel had failed to scoop up.

lines.japanese: 小片と言ったって、はたらくくるまレベルの話。中にはヒトを殺せそうなサイズの大物だって残ってる。
lines.english: I say *small*, but only by the standards of heavy machinery. Some of the big ones looked capable of killing a man.

lines.japanese: 俺は大小のそれをひょいひょい拾って、一輪車の受け皿に放る、放る、放る。
lines.english: I scooped them up, large and small, and tossed them into the wheelbarrow. Toss, toss, toss.

lines.japanese: 結構な量だけど、ひとりで黙々と汗を流せばいいだけだから、さして苦じゃない。
lines.english: There was plenty of it, but all I had to do was sweat in silence by myself. I didn't mind.

lines.japanese: 少し体が温まってきたころ、俺はいったん腰を伸ばし、軍手ごしに指の関節を鳴らして気合を入れた。
lines.english: Once my body had warmed a little, I straightened my back, cracked my knuckles inside the gloves, and psyched myself up.

lines.japanese: いちばんデカい、魚市場で見たクロマグロみたいな砕片を両手で掴んだ。イイカンジで重い。上等だ。
lines.english: With both hands I seized the largest fragment, a slab like a bluefin tuna I'd once seen at a fish market. Just the right kind of heavy. Excellent.
“Hrragh!”

lines.japanese: 腰をひねって投げいれた。削岩ドリルにも負けない轟音が鼓膜を震わせる。よし、ノッてきた。
lines.english: Twisting at the waist, I hurled it in. A crash to rival the rock drill shook my eardrums. Good. I was finding my rhythm.

lines.japanese: 「はっ！」
lines.english: “Hah!”

lines.japanese: 「ふゥっ！」
lines.english: “Hnh!”

lines.japanese: 「ほおォっ！」
lines.english: “Hoooh!”

lines.japanese: 「うるァーッ！」
lines.english: “Rrrah!”

lines.japanese: 次々と、機械のような一連の動きで放りこんだ。
lines.english: One after another, I threw them in with the rhythm of a machine.

lines.japanese: こういうのはリズムと集中が肝心。冬の寒さを吹きとばすには、大ぶりに体を動かすのがいちば──
lines.english: Rhythm and concentration were everything in this kind of work. The best way to drive off the winter cold was to put your whole body into a great big—

lines.japanese: 「うるせえよ飛び込み！　もっと静かにやれバカ！」
lines.english: “Shut the hell up, temp! Keep it down, idiot!”

lines.japanese: ──怒られてしまった。
lines.english: —and I got yelled at.

lines.japanese: 「すんません」
lines.english: “Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 俺はヘルメットの頭を下げた。下げたから顔は隠れる。
lines.english: I bowed my helmeted head. That hid my face.

lines.japanese: 「おまえの方がうるせえよ」
lines.english: “You're louder than me.”

lines.japanese: もちろん表には出さない。いや、いくら俺だって、仕事となれば口は慎むよ。
lines.english: Naturally, I kept that to myself. Even I watched my mouth when I was on the job.

lines.japanese: はあ……動いていないと冷えるよな。体とか、いろいろさ。
lines.english: Haaah... If I stopped moving, all sorts of things started getting cold. My body, for one.
